name: Aflatoxin Contamination
description: A fungal contamination issue producing highly toxic aflatoxins in groundnut. It occurs both pre-harvest and post-harvest, caused by Aspergillus fungi. Aflatoxins are carcinogenic and pose serious health risks to humans and livestock.
symptoms: Yellow-green mold growth on kernels (visible after shelling)
Mold may not always be visible — contamination can be invisible
No visible plant symptoms in the field during growing season
causes: Aspergillus flavus and Aspergillus parasiticus fungi
High soil temperatures during pod fill
Insect damage to pods providing entry points
Delayed harvest leaving mature pods in soil
Improper drying (high moisture content at storage)
Poor storage conditions with high humidity and temperature
treatments: No treatment for contaminated seeds — discard affected batches
Dry groundnuts to below 8% moisture immediate after harvest
Sort and remove visibly damaged or moldy kernels
Use aflatoxin binders in animal feed (not for human consumption)
prevention: Irrigate during drought periods to reduce plant stress
Harvest at optimal maturity — do not delay harvest
Sun-dry groundnuts on clean mats or tarpaulins immediately after harvest
Dry to safe moisture level (<8%) within 48 hours of harvest
Store in clean, dry, well-ventilated conditions
Use resistant groundnut varieties (ICGV series with aflatoxin resistance)
Apply biocontrol (non-toxigenic Aspergillus strains) such as AflaSafe
Practice crop rotation to reduce soil inoculum
